data.title: Article 370 abrogation ended separatism among Kashmiri youth: Amit Shah
data.description:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said that the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth, and not a single local youth in the Valley is now involved in terrorism after 35 years of violence and unrest.

He was addressing an event at Police Training Centre in Banderdewa near Itanagar in which the President's Police Colour was conferred to Arunachal Pradesh Police.

"After over 35 years of violence, not a single local youth of Kashmir Valley is now involved in terrorism," he said.

Recalling the troubled 90s, he said the situation in Kashmir Valley has undergone a sea change after the abrogation of Article 370.

 

About criticism by opposition parties that the constitutional provision had no connection with terrorism, Shah said developments in the Valley have demonstrated otherwise.

He said the change in the Kashmir Valley was brought about not merely by eliminating terrorists but also by ending the atmosphere of discrimination and alienation among the youth of Kashmir.

Development activities undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014 had further strengthened the prospects of lasting peace, he added.

Shah said the transformation in Kashmir was a matter of immense pride for the country and reflected the sacrifices and dedication of security forces and intelligence agencies.

Recalling the turbulent 90s, Shah said terrorism was at its peak and there were doubts about how long the country would be able to hold on to Kashmir.

"Even the chief minister of the state had left for England, while security forces, through their courage and sacrifices, ensured that the Valley remained connected with the rest of the country," he said.

"Today, from this sacred land of Parshuram ji, I want to tell the entire nation with pride that the abrogation of Article 370 has brought an end to the sense of separatism among the youth of Kashmir. This is reflected in the fact that today, not a single Kashmiri youth is involved in terrorism in Kashmir Valley," he said.

Shah said the change in Kashmir was not limited to the elimination of terrorists but also marked a shift in the mindset of the younger generation, with separatist tendencies giving way to hopes of peace and development.

He said development in the Valley had gained momentum under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014, adding that the coming years held great promise for Kashmir.

The home minister expressed confidence that the transformation in the Valley would pave the way for lasting peace and prosperity, asserting that the experience demonstrated the government's commitment to strengthening national security and promoting development across the country.

data.title: Noel Tata questions Chandra's reappointment, seeks recording of Sep meeting
data.description:
Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata has questioned the validity of N Chandrasekaran's five-year reappointment as executive chairman of Tata Sons, alleging procedural irregularities in the decision and disputing the voting process at the company's September 17 board meeting, The Economic Times reported on Saturday.
 
According to the ET report, in a seven-page letter dated November 20 to Tata Sons Company Secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay, copied to all directors, Noel sought detailed written responses by November 25, a day before the holding company's next board meeting scheduled for November 26.
 
Noel, who is also a director of Tata Sons, argued that Chandrasekaran's reappointment was moved without prior notice and without a formal recommendation from the company's Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC).
 
 
The NRC, which met on September 3, had only asked Chandrasekaran to reconsider his decision to step down, Noel said. The committee's minutes did not record any subsequent meeting or a formal recommendation to the board on his reappointment, he added.
 
He also challenged the validity of the voting process, citing Article 121 of Tata Sons' Articles of Association (AoA), which, according to him, requires the affirmative vote of a majority of directors appointed under Article 104B who are present at the meeting.
 
Only two such directors attended the September 17 meeting, with one voting against the resolution, Noel said. He disputed the chairman's use of a casting vote to break what the draft minutes described as a tie between the Trusts' nominee directors. He also questioned why a selection committee under Article 118 of the AoA had not been constituted for the appointment process.

Demand for recording of Sep 17 meeting

Noel has also intensified his demand for access to the audio and video recording of the September 17 board meeting.
 
Tata Sons, in its November 9 response, had confirmed that the meeting was recorded but declined to share the footage, arguing that it was meant only to assist in preparing the minutes and did not need to be retained or disclosed to directors.
 
Noel said directors were entitled to inspect company records in electronic form and that Article 129 of the AoA did not exclude such access. He sought written confirmation that the complete, unedited recording existed, details of its custody and access, and an assurance that it would be preserved until the dispute was resolved.
 
Warning that any deletion or alteration after September 18, when he first sought preservation of the recording, could amount to the "deliberate destruction of evidence", Noel offered to inspect it at Bombay House, Tata Sons' headquarters, in the presence of an adviser.
 
Noel further asked that the September 17 meeting's minutes be finalised only after the board had considered his objections. He also sought that Chandrasekaran not participate in discussions concerning his own reappointment.

Questions over potential conflicts of interest

The letter separately raised questions about potential conflicts of interest involving Chandrasekaran and Tata Sons director Venu Srinivasan.
 
Noel said Chandrasekaran's April 2025 disclosure listed his wife and son as partners and directors in Hanno entities but did not disclose any dealings with TVS Motor Co.
 
This assumes significance, he said, in light of reports that TVS Motor had leased land to Hanno One in June 2025. Noel also questioned whether Srinivasan, who was part of the committee that assessed Chandrasekaran's performance and recommended his remuneration and reappointment, had disclosed any potential conflict arising from the relationship.

data.title: Google announces $5 mn funding for IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research
data.description:
Technology giant Google on Saturday said it will provide IIT Kharagpur with $5 million, about ₹46 crore, to develop and accelerate advanced AI research.

Speaking on the 75th anniversary of IIT Kharagpur, Director Suman Chakraborty said that the fund support for applied AI research has been envisaged by the institute's alumnus and Google CEO Sundar Pichai.

"Google is providing the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur) with $5 million in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research, while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent," the company said in a blog.

The funding will support the institute's researchers and students across three core pillars, comprising advanced AI research, educational opportunities and AI capacity building.

 

Under advanced AI research, the fund will support tackling critical, real-world challenges by deploying AI for Indic languages, materials science, agriculture, and educational technology.

As part of educational opportunities, it will support expansion of AI training and curriculum development for students and faculty.

The fund will support the institute's AI frameworks and tooling to elevate the technological ecosystem across the campus.

"IIT Kharagpur is driving groundbreaking work in areas like Indic languages, agriculture, and education, and Google is excited to help accelerate this impact with a new partnership. Looking forward to seeing this collaboration shape the path for the next generation of students, just as IIT Kharagpur shaped my own," Pichai said.

He said India is increasingly at the forefront of innovation; programmes like this will help implement Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision that the benefits of AI reach everyone in India.

data.title: Cyclone Akvan disrupts air traffic, 14 flights cancelled in Ranchi
data.description:
As many as 14 flights were cancelled at the Birsa Munda Airport in Ranchi on Saturday due to inclement weather triggered by cyclone 'Akvan', an official said.

Jharkhand has been experiencing cloudy weather coupled with light rain since Friday under the influence of the cyclone.

For safe landing or take-off, a visibility between 1,200 and 1,500 metres is required.

"The visibility at Ranchi airport was around 1,000 metres until 1pm," Airport Director Vinod Kumar told PTI.

He said that 14 scheduled flights were cancelled due to bad weather.

data.title: EPF is becoming a retirement income plan. Is it a better one?
data.description:
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) board in New Delhi on Thursday (November 19) approved a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP), the Labour Ministry said. Retirees can take savings in instalments, monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, instead of one lump sum.

 

The ministry says the plan is meant to supplement pension benefits. It is voluntary and will first be open to members above 55 with over Rs 5 lakh saved.

 

The board also eased withdrawal rules and approved in principle investing up to 3 per cent of fresh yearly inflows in alternative investment funds (AIFs), the ministry said.

 

Table 1: What the EPFO board changed

 
 

 

How long will the money last?

 

Vivek Iyer, partner and financial services risk advisory leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, says the plan addresses “a long-standing gap in India’s retirement system”. India has focused on saving for retirement, he says, but offered little help with turning those savings into income.

 

The advisory firm’s illustration shows how it could work. A retiree at 58 with Rs 50 lakh takes Rs 40,000 a month. If the balance keeps earning 8.25 per cent, the money lasts about 24 years, to age 82.

 

Unlike an annuity, Iyer says, the plan lets members “keep ownership and flexibility over their corpus”. If the member dies at 68, about Rs 39.6 lakh passes to the nominee, the illustration shows.

 

Everything hinges on interest. The ministry says the remaining money will keep generating returns. Iyer says whether it keeps earning the EPF rate “is what makes the plan attractive”.

 

Kunal Kabra, founder of Kustodian.Life, a provident fund recovery firm, says EPF interest stops three years after retirement under current rules. On Grant Thornton’s example, that would cut the 24 years to about 13, Business Standard’s calculation shows.

 

“If the interest still stops, then this option doesn’t make any sense,” Kabra says. It is not yet clear whether the balance under the new plan escapes that rule.

 

The ministry has not said how instalments will be taxed. It says a corresponding Income Tax Act amendment is being taken up with the Finance Ministry. Kabra says interest earned after leaving a job is taxable.

 

Iyer also lists tax clarity among the choices that will decide how useful the plan is. Members need “certainty on how each instalment will be taxed”, he says.

 

Do easier withdrawals undercut the plan?

 

A SWP only helps if there is a corpus left at retirement. Only 10 per cent of the balance now has to stay in the account, down from 25 per cent, as per the latest press release. The wait for final withdrawal after losing a job also drops from 12 months to two.

 

Kabra welcomes the shorter wait after job loss. But he is “not too convinced if it would be used more or if it would be misused more.”

 

What about alternative funds?

 

The board approved in principle putting up to 3 per cent of fresh yearly inflows into AIFs, initially through government-backed entities and within the existing overall investment ceiling, the ministry said. It says the aim is to diversify EPFO’s investments, with safeguards and oversight.  

NPS has been moving the same way. Its Retirement Income Schemes, launched in May, let retirees draw monthly, quarterly or annual payouts from the lump sum they retain, while it stays invested.

 

Its regulator, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), is also opening pension savings to AIFs, including private equity and private debt. EPFO’s approval in principle takes EPF in the same direction.

 

If executed well, Iyer says, the plan could become India’s default way of drawing retirement income. Above all, he says, it treats retirement “as a stream of income rather than a single payout”.

data.title: 'Look at India': Trump cites 7% growth to criticise US Fed's rate policy
data.description:
US President Donald Trump on Friday cited India's 7 per cent economic growth to criticise the US Federal Reserve for keeping interest rates high, claiming that the American economy could expand by as much as 20 per cent if borrowing costs were reduced.
 
Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump accused the Federal Reserve of following a politically motivated approach to monetary policy and alleged that it raised interest rates whenever the US reported strong economic figures, rather than lowering them to support further growth.
 
"Interest rates are too high because we have a very political Fed. I'm not blaming the chairman, but the fact that we have a very political Fed. Whenever we announce good numbers, they raise the interest rates. They do that for a reason. It should be the opposite," Trump said, according to news agency ANI.
 
 
He argued that stronger economic performance should allow the US to borrow at lower rates, as favourable financial indicators would make the country a more creditworthy borrower.
 
"When we have these great numbers, you shouldn't keep raising the rates. You should lower rates because we're a better credit. We would have a GDP of 15 or 20 per cent, not 4 per cent. We'd pay off the debt very rapidly. That's the way it should work. But we do it in reverse," he said.

Trump draws comparison with India

Citing India's economic performance, Trump pointed to its 7 per cent GDP growth and what he described as relatively low interest rates set by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
"If you look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a 7 per cent GDP. We'd have a 14 per cent, 15 per cent, maybe even a 20 per cent GDP," he said.
 
The US President also questioned why the country should not have the lowest interest rates globally, given its economic influence and role in supporting other economies.
 
"We're the country that makes other countries successful. Some of them are considered financial elite, but they are not. They are only elite because of us. So we should have the lowest," he said.

Fed's inflation concerns

Trump's criticism comes as US inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's long-term target of 2 per cent. Annual personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation stood at 3.6 per cent in September, while core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, was 3.1 per cent.
 
The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points in September to a target range of 3.75-4 per cent. It kept the range unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, citing elevated inflation. Two policymakers favoured another 25-basis-point increase.

India's inflation pressures build

India, meanwhile, is facing rising inflationary pressures, with retail inflation breaching the RBI's upper tolerance limit of 6 per cent in October. Wholesale price inflation also rose to its highest level under the current series, driven largely by higher fuel and power prices.
 
The inflation numbers have strengthened expectations of further monetary tightening. The RBI raised the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent in October, and economists widely expect it to raise rates by another 25 basis points at each of its two remaining MPC meetings in the current cycle, in December and February.

data.title: Adani Energy to supply 2,500 MW renewable energy to West Bengal discom
data.description:
Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) on Saturday said its wholly-owned subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions Ltd (PTSL) has bagged a project to supply up to 2,500 MW of renewable energy to West Bengal discom WBSEDCL for 25 years.

The Letter of Award (LoA) from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co Ltd (WBSEDCL) is for the supply of 1,750 MW of renewable energy round-the-clock for a period of 25 years. The LoA provides a 750 MW green shoe option, which, upon exercise, would take the aggregate contracted capacity to 2,500 MW, AESL said in a statement.

The award follows a competitive bidding process. Power supply is scheduled to begin from July 1, 2028, for 1,750 MW capacity and from April 1, 2029, for 750 MW, once the green shoe option is exercised, it said "Round-the-clock renewable power will be critical to India's energy transition, combining the sustainability of renewables and optimising transmission systems usage. This significant order win strengthens our commitment to deliver scalable energy solutions, and allows us to partner with WBSEDCL in supporting West Bengal's long-term sustinable power needs.

 

"PTSL is rapidly emerging as a partner of choice for bulk power consumers, with the ability to structure bespoke and scalable solutions around their specific energy requirements," said Kandarp Patel, CEO, AESL.

The order represents a significant addition to PTSL's expanding portfolio of energy solutions. While it has tied-up ~ 4.6 GW of solar & wind, and 3.5 GWh of battery energy storage system capacity on the sourcing side, it is steadily stitching the supply side by augmenting long-term supply contracts with bulk consumers like industries, data centres, commercial entities, and discoms.

Part of Adani Group, AESL has a presence in power transmission, distribution, smart metering, and cooling solutions.

AESL is the country's largest private transmission company with a cumulative transmission network of 30,683 ckm and 1,46,585 MVA transformation capacity.

AESL serves approximately 13 million retail consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the industrial hub of Mundra SEZ. AESL is also ramping up its smart metering business and is on course to become India's leading smart metering integrator.

data.title: Heller Industries sets up India's first reflow oven mfg plant in Gujarat
data.description:
US-based Heller Industries Inc on Friday inaugurated its first Indian manufacturing facility near Ahmedabad, becoming the first global reflow oven maker to produce the critical semiconductor and electronics assembly equipment locally in the country.

Operated through its subsidiary Heller Thermal Systems Private Limited (HTS) at Gallops Industrial Park in Rajoda, the 30,000 sq ft facility has been established with the strategic and operational support of long-term Indian partner NMTronics India Pvt Ltd, a company statement said. The plant is designed with a production capacity of 40 ovens per month.

HTS plans to dispatch 18 ovens in 2026, scaling up to 146 units in 2027 and 180 units in 2028, by which time one in every three ovens built at the facility will be exported to markets across the US, Europe, and Southeast Asia, the statement said. International exports from the plant are scheduled to commence in December 2026, while custom and semi-custom oven manufacturing will begin by March 2027.

 

To support this expansion, HTS will double its workforce from 30 to 60 employees by 2028, while generating an equal number of indirect jobs across its domestic supplier network.

"India has become one of the most important electronics manufacturing markets in the world, and our ability to become the first global reflow oven maker to build here is a direct result of our enduring partnership with NMTronics," Heller Industries CEO David Heller said.

Soni Saran Singh, Founder, MD and CEO of NMTronics India and Director of Heller Thermal Systems, noted that as Gujarat emerges as a premier hub for semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, building these critical systems locally will help reduce dependence on imported equipment.

Reflow ovens are core to printed circuit board assemblies used in smartphones, EV controllers, AI servers, and semiconductor packages. Until now, global reflow ovens operating in India, including roughly 400 Heller units, were entirely imported. The new plant also features a customer training room and a live demonstration floor with a complete Surface Mount Technology line for on-site production trials.

data.title: India has shown it can break limits, unlock possibilities: PM Modi
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said India has shown over the past 12 years that breaking barriers in thinking can help the country realise its potential, create opportunities and empower the poor.

Addressing the platinum jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur, the country's first Indian Institute of Technology, here, Modi said India had declared "loud and clear" its resolve to "break the limits and unlock the possibilities".

"The nation only understands its capacity when it breaks its limits and unlocks the possibilities," he said.

The Prime Minister said that over the last 12 years, his government had worked to break existing limitations and empower the poor.

 

"Earlier, people used to talk about removing poverty from the Red Fort, but they never did anything except making files," he said.

Referring to a World Bank report, Modi claimed that around 50 crore people had come out of poverty in the last 12-13 years, describing it as a result of a change in the country's approach and thinking.

"The country discovers its capabilities only when it breaks the boundaries of thinking. Over the past few years, India has shown exactly that," he said.

Modi said West Bengal was a land where ideas had gained strength, and national movements had taken shape, adding that IIT Kharagpur stood on a site that once housed a detention camp for freedom fighters.

He urged students to draw inspiration from the lives, thoughts and activities of freedom fighters who were detained at the site.

"Imagine what the freedom fighters who stayed here must have talked about and thought about all day," he told the students, adding that their ideas and sacrifices continued to inspire generations.

The PM said the institution had completed 75 years of its journey and achieved several milestones during this period.

India, too, had witnessed tremendous transformation over these decades, moving "from bullock carts to bullet trains, from postal letters to social media messages", he said.

As India moves towards the goal of a 'Viksit Bharat', IIT Kharagpur's 75 years of experience would play a significant role in the country's development and innovation ecosystem, Modi said.

The institute's contribution to education, research and technological advancement would be important in shaping India's future, he added.

data.title: GST Network adds metro rail as fifth mode of transport in e-way bill system
data.description:
The GST Network (GSTN) has added metro rail as a new mode of transport in the e-way bill system.

Currently, the facility has also been released in the "Sandbox environment" for API users to test and make necessary changes to their systems. Its roll-out in the live API environment will be announced separately, GSTN, which manages the IT backbone of Goods and Services Tax, said.

The facility follows a government notification dated October 26.

With this addition, the e-way bill system now has five modes of transport: Road, Rail, Air, Ship and Metro Rail.

Under the Goods and Services Tax (GST), the e-way bill is mandatory for transiting goods valued at ₹50,000 and above, both inter- and intra-state.

 

GSTN, in an advisory issued on November 20, said the new option is available to web users for generating e-way bills and updating transport details.

Users transporting goods through metro rail must select it as the mode of transport and enter the mandatory transport document number.

The new option is also available for vehicle updates and generation and re-generation of consolidated e-way bills.

"API users are advised to undertake the necessary changes and complete testing before its roll-out in production," GSTN said in an advisory.

In the GST system, API users are businesses or transporters who use software connected directly to the GST portal to generate e-way bills and carry out other GST-related activities, instead of logging in and doing it manually on the portal.
